retained_original_metadata.title: The generic square_q algebra has a unique cyclic NIL module, which is irreducible and infinite-dimensional through its explicit affine-sl2 q-shuffle realization
retained_original_metadata.author: Sarah Post; Paul Terwilliger
retained_original_metadata.source_title: An Infinite-Dimensional square(q)-Module Obtained from the q-Shuffle Algebra for Affine sl(2)
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof connects a free-word quotient and a q-shuffle model using an explicit graded intertwiner whose invertibility is proved through a cyclic word operator. It combines lowering-operator minimal-degree arguments with generation in a different isomorphic model to establish irreducibility. A universal NIL word-map and kernel argument then prove uniqueness, rather than merely checking that a displayed operator table satisfies relations.

proof_review.note: Read the complete NIL uniqueness chain15.4-15.7 and the following irreducibility/infinite-dimension conclusion; full III-to-IV intertwiner construction12.4-12.23, q-Serre quotient and orthogonal-kernel supports6.2-6.5/9.3-9.4/10.3-10.4, and irreducibility14.6-14.8. The exact word-operator formulas and mixed-generator identity are supplied; their commutator checks are the author's explicit routine calculations. Rosso's q-shuffle kernel theorem is identified established background. Physical page24 model tables were rendered and viewed. Only the unique NIL isomorphism class is selected, not sixteen model variants or the grading sequence theorem.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem15.7 together with the immediately following Definition15.8/unlabelled conclusion: F any field, q nonzero and not a root of unity; square_q has four cyclic generators with exactly the q-Weyl and opposite q-Serre relations of Definition13.2. A NIL module is generated by a nonzero vector annihilated by x1 and x3. There is a unique such isomorphism class, realized by the stated q-shuffle module, and it is irreducible and infinite-dimensional. No root-of-unity, arbitrary cyclic module or sixteen distinct classes claim is added.
